newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch oppose cherry picking in rail competition.
newsitem.headline: Dutch oppose cherry picking in rail competition.

text.p: Dutch Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma said on Wednesday that she would not allow cherry picking in rail competition.

"I'm very much in favour of free competition. But it cannot be that some new company is selecting nice services that are currently generating profits at (state-owned) Dutch Railways...We ask Dutch Railways to invest in loss-making lines too," she said in a interview with daily newspaper Algemeen Dagblad, that was confirmed by a Ministry's spokeswoman.
This summer Dutch Railways met its first post-war competitor when rival Lovers Rail launched a beach-express from Amsterdam to seaport IJmuiden.
Last week the new company submitted requests for five more services in the urban heart of the Netherlands where Dutch Railways runs most of its profitable lines.
Dutch Railways has repeatedly expressed objections to cherry picking by possible new rivals and suggested that the Dutch state would offer entire lines.
On these lines train companies would then have to offer a full range of express and local services for the entire day.
Dutch Railways is currently financing losses on local lines with profits generated on intercity services.
Minister Jorritsma will submit her proposals for free rail comeptition to parliament by late October.
